$comment: Landing-section → kestrel-behavior map for the refresh-from-kestrel skill.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: at a version bump the skill has to answer 'which part of
getkestrel.dev now describes kestrel wrongly?'. The changelog is the INDEX of what
changed; this file is the reverse index — for each thing the landing page claims,
it records where that claim lives and which kestrel behaviours it depends on. The
skill crosses the two: a changelog entry that touches a surface's behaviour is a
candidate for a copy edit or a screenshot refresh.
HOW TO KEEP IT CURRENT: the landing copy is still in flux (#5, #19). When you edit
layouts/index.html, update the matching surface here in the same change — the copy
quote, the asserts, and the keywords. Treat this as documentation of the landing's
factual claims, not as a lookup table to be trusted blindly. `keywords` only drive
the script's *candidate* hints; the real mapping is editorial judgement (see the
role model in SKILL.md). A keyword hit is a prompt to go look, never a verdict.
SCHEMA (per surface): id, label, kind, source, anchor, asserts[], keywords[],

roleModel.publisher: Writes and sends the newsletter (the person running a publication).
roleModel.developer: Deploys and operates the app on their own Cloudflare account. getkestrel.dev's /docs are the developer/setup guides — this is the audience the landing's 'self-host' framing addresses.
roleModel.reader: Subscribes to and reads a newsletter.
roleModel.note: kestrel retired the old 'operator' word into publisher + developer. A mechanical find-replace gets this wrong (see PR #27, which corrected a bad operator->publisher edit to operator->developer). When a changelog entry names a role or a role-specific action, decide which of these three it means before touching copy.

surfaces.label: Hero app-preview screenshot
asserts: The dashboard looks as pictured: subscriber counts, a scheduled issue, drafts, and sent issues.
The editor/composer chrome (tabs, toolbars, notices, alerts) matches the current app.

regen.prerequisite: A seeded kestrel dev server at the NEW ref must be running: in a kestrel checkout at <new> run `npm run dev` then `npm run seed`, then `npm run shots` here. See scripts/shots.mjs.

surfaces.notes: This is the surface most likely to go stale and the one a docs-only re-sync will never catch. ANY editor/dashboard UI change in the changelog (new tab, moved page, new notice, removed alert) makes the shipped PNGs suspect. Regenerating needs a running v0.2.0-or-later dev server, so if one isn't available, FLAG it as a follow-up (#19) rather than silently leaving stale images — that is exactly what the v0.1.0→v0.2.0 bump did.

surfaces.label: Hero lead paragraph
surfaces.anchor: Write in Markdown, preview the exact email, schedule with a cancelable review window
asserts: You write in Markdown.
You preview the exact email that will be sent.
You schedule with a cancelable review window.
You send to your subscribers.
You keep the list, the consent record, the delivery record, and a permanent per-issue archive.
surfaces.notes: The one-sentence promise of the whole app. A changelog entry that renames or removes any of these verbs (write/preview/schedule/send/archive) or the ownership nouns (list/consent/delivery/archive) lands here first.

surfaces.label: Ownership — 'You keep what matters' (4 cards)
asserts: The list: subscribers live in your own D1 database; query or export any time.
The consent: every subscription is double opt-in, with confirmation and unsubscribe recorded.
The delivery: each send records who received which issue, plus suppressions from hard bounces and spam complaints.
The archive: every issue gets a lasting public page on your own domain.
surfaces.notes: These are data-ownership guarantees, not UI. They change rarely, and when they do it is usually a Breaking or a Changed entry about consent, suppression, storage, or the archive.

surfaces.label: How it works — write/preview/schedule/send/archive (5 steps)
asserts: Write in Markdown in the web editor or via Claude; a stale save is rejected rather than clobbered.
Preview the exact rendered email HTML and plain-text; send yourself a test first.
Schedule behind a cancelable countdown; a Cron Trigger drives the sweep.
Send only to confirmed subscribers; the send loop is idempotent so it never double-sends; bounces and complaints suppress on their own.
Archive each sent issue as a permanent, indexable page on your domain.
surfaces.notes: This restates the flow with mechanism detail, so it overlaps the hero-lead and the under-the-hood spec list. A behaviour change to any step (e.g. the schedule/send-now flow, the send loop, the stale-save rejection) should be checked against the exact wording here.

surfaces.label: Under the hood — tech-stack chips
asserts: The stack is: TypeScript, Cloudflare Workers, D1, R2, Cron Triggers, SES, Resend.
surfaces.notes: The literal dependency/provider list. A new provider adapter → add a chip; a dropped or renamed dependency → remove/rename one. This is the surface a 'new provider' change (the issue's own example) maps to.

surfaces.label: Under the hood — engineering spec list (6 items)
asserts: One API, two clients: a single HTTP API; the web editor and Claude are just clients; nothing the editor can do is off-API.
Optimistic concurrency: edits are revision-checked (If-Match / ETag); a stale write is rejected with 409.
Idempotent send loop: the scheduled sweep is safe to retry and resumes without re-mailing anyone.
Three isolated environments: dev, staging, production each get their own database, storage, and mail transport.
Swappable email provider: SES or Resend in production; a fake in-memory transport for local dev and tests; one variable.
Access-gated admin: authoring behind Cloudflare Access; reader pages public, gated by unguessable per-subscriber tokens.
surfaces.notes: The most technical claims, and the ones most exactly worded (409, If-Match/ETag, 'one variable', 'three environments'). A changelog entry that changes an interface contract, the environment set, the provider seam, or the auth model needs the exact wording here re-checked, not just the gist.

surfaces.label: Self-host quickstart commands
surfaces.anchor: From clone to a running instance
asserts: The shortest path is: git clone; npm install; cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars; npm run dev (http://localhost:8787); npm run seed.
A real deployed instance additionally needs a Cloudflare account, one Access application, an email provider (SES or Resend), and sending-domain DNS.
surfaces.notes: The only place the landing pins literal commands and a port. A renamed npm script, a changed dev port, a new required setup step, or a changed env file name breaks this. Cross-check with the synced /docs/ setup guides, which cover the full deploy.
